forces.title: Government support for domestic MedTech manufacturing.
forces.description: Government policies like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme and the National Medical Devices Policy 2023 are accelerating investments and strengthening India's medical device manufacturing ecosystem. This includes specific allowances for 100% FDI in the sector, with consumables attracting significant investment, fostering local production and reducing import dependency for medical supplies.

forces.title: Increasing domestic production and cost competitiveness.
forces.description: India has observed a significant structural shift in medical device production, with domestic market share increasing from 10% to 30% of total requirements in the last five years. Even complex Class-C devices are now manufactured domestically at 10-40% cheaper costs. This trend, bolstered by government initiatives, directly impacts the Medical Supplies & Consumables sector by enhancing affordability and self-reliance.

forces.title: Expanding healthcare infrastructure and patient access.
forces.description: The rising number of medical facilities, including private hospitals adding thousands of beds annually, coupled with government initiatives like Ayushman Bharat expanding healthcare access and insurance coverage, directly boosts the demand for medical supplies and consumables. Increased patient footfall and procedures necessitate a higher volume of single-use items and wound care products.

forces.title: Regulatory clarity for medical device classification.
forces.description: The Health Ministry of India has classified medical devices, including consumables like surgical dressings, catheters, and alcohol swabs, into four risk classes (A, B, C, D) under medical device and IVD regulations. This regulatory clarity provides a structured framework for manufacturers and suppliers of medical supplies and consumables, aiding compliance, quality assurance, and market entry, fostering orderly sector growth.

forces.title: Growth in healthcare workforce driving demand.
forces.description: India's healthcare workforce, having exceeded 6 million in CY24 and projected to add over 6.3 million more jobs by CY30, signifies a substantial expansion in healthcare delivery capacity. A larger medical workforce directly translates to more patient interactions, procedures, and institutional activity, thereby increasing the overall consumption of medical supplies and consumables.

viewpoints.title: India's medical device sector poised for global presence and innovation.
viewpoints.description: India's medical device industry, encompassing consumables, is strengthening its global standing through adoption of new-generation technologies like AI and predictive diagnostics. This boost in innovation and job growth reflects sustained global demand for Indian medical devices and the country's strengthening manufacturing and export ecosystem. Policy-makers anticipate significant expansion, positioning India as a key global player.

viewpoints.title: Domestic Medical Device Production Increasing, Offering Cost Advantage.
viewpoints.description: India's medical device sector, which includes consumables, has seen domestic production market share increase from 10% to 30% of requirements over the last five years. Even for complex Class-C devices, 20% are now manufactured domestically at 10-40% lower costs. This highlights a structural shift towards self-reliance ('Atmanirbhar') and enhanced cost-effectiveness, positioning India strongly in the global MedTech landscape.

viewpoints.title: Government Promoting Affordable Consumables Through Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
viewpoints.description: The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, with a target of 25,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by March 2027, explicitly offers 315 types of devices and consumables. This government initiative aims to promote affordable, quality generic healthcare, directly supporting the volume-driven, lower-margin business model of medical supplies and consumables by increasing access and affordability.

demand_drivers.description: The overall healthcare sector in India is experiencing increasing demand, driven by factors like rising income levels, an aging population, growing health awareness, and a shift towards preventive healthcare, directly boosting the need for medical supplies and consumables.

Increased penetration of health insurance supports affordability and accessibility of healthcare services, leading to higher utilization of medical facilities and, consequently, greater demand for medical supplies and consumables.

The expansion of medical facilities, including private hospitals adding thousands of beds, and supportive government policies are enhancing healthcare infrastructure, which directly drives increased consumption of single-use medical items, wound care products, and other consumables.

Government initiatives like the PLI Scheme, National Medical Devices Policy 2023, and promotion of affordable healthcare through Jan Aushadhi Kendras (offering devices/consumables) are fostering domestic manufacturing, investment, and wider access, stimulating demand for medical supplies.

market_sizing.methodology: Derived from the total Indian medical device market valuation (US$15.2 billion in 2025) and its projected growth to US$50.1 billion by 2030, as stated on page 54. The share of 'disposables & consumables' within this market is explicitly segmented as 26.5%, as detailed on page 49.
